items.sentence1: Without the satnav, we would have got completely lost in the mountains.
items.after: the satnav, we would have got completely lost in the mountains.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'without' in a third conditional becomes 'If it had not (hadn't)', with the past perfect because the situation is in the past. Part 2: the fixed structure is 'if it hadn't been for' + noun.
explanation.cs: Část 1: without ve třetím kondicionálu nahradíme 'If it had not / hadn't' (minulost, proto past perfect). Část 2: ustálená vazba if it hadn't been for + podstatné jméno = nebýt (čeho).

items.sentence1: Engineers will have finished the repairs to the bridge by the time we arrive.

explanation.en: Part 1: the action will be complete before a future moment, so the future perfect 'will have' stays. Part 2: the bridge is the object of the action, so the passive 'been repaired' follows. 'Will be repaired' loses the idea of completion before we arrive.
explanation.cs: Část 1: děj bude dokončen před určitým okamžikem v budoucnosti, proto future perfect: will have. Část 2: most opravuje někdo jiný, proto pasivum: been repaired. 'Will be repaired' neříká, že oprava bude hotová už před naším příjezdem.

items.sentence1: 'If I were you, I'd book a table in advance,' the receptionist told us.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'If I were you, I'd...' is advice, reported with 'recommended (that) we'. Part 2: the verb after it is the base form ('book') or 'should book'. 'Recommended booking' is also good English but has only 2 words, and 'recommended us to book' is widely considered incorrect.
explanation.cs: Část 1: 'If I were you, I'd…' je rada, kterou převedeme jako recommended (that) we. Část 2: následuje holý infinitiv (book) nebo should book. 'Recommended booking' je správně, ale má jen 2 slova; 'recommended us to book' se považuje za chybu.

items.sentence1: The hotel was cheap, and it was very comfortable as well.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'and ... as well' becomes the paired linker 'not only', placed directly before the first quality, 'cheap'. Part 2: the second half is introduced by 'but (also)'. There is no inversion here, because 'not only' does not start the sentence.
explanation.cs: Část 1: 'and … as well' nahradíme párovou spojkou not only, která stojí přímo před první vlastností (cheap). Část 2: druhou část uvádí but (also). Inverze zde není, protože not only nestojí na začátku věty.

items.sentence1: I completely forgot to water my neighbour's plants while she was away.
items.after: my neighbour's plants while she was away.
fullAnswers: completely slipped my mind to water

explanation.en: Part 1: 'I forgot' becomes the idiom 'it slipped my mind', where the thing forgotten is the subject, not the person. Part 2: the forgotten action follows as 'to water'. 'Completely' may be kept before 'slipped'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: I forgot = idiom it slipped my mind (vypadlo mi to z hlavy); podmětem není člověk, ale věc. Část 2: zapomenutou činnost připojíme infinitivem: to water. Slovo completely můžeme ponechat před slipped.

items.sentence1: We took a lot of food with us, but that was unnecessary because the hostel had a café.
items.after: so much food with us, as the hostel had a café.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'need not have' says we did something that turned out to be unnecessary. 'Needn't' would change the key word, so write 'need not'. 'Did not need to' and 'had no need to' are accepted, as the context shows that we took the food. Part 2: after 'need not have' use the past participle 'taken'; after 'need to' use the base form 'take'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: need not have + příčestí = udělali jsme něco zbytečně. Tvar needn't by změnil klíčové slovo, proto need not. Uznává se i did not need to / had no need to, protože z kontextu je jasné, že jídlo jsme vzali. Část 2: po need not have příčestí taken, po need to holý infinitiv take.
